issue: fs.readFileSync on every MCP tool invocation (list/get/set/adjust)
estimated_impact: features.json is ~16KB / 294 lines. Every tool call blocks the Node event loop for the duration of the sync read + JSON.parse (~1-3ms cold, sub-ms warm via OS page cache). Under the HTTP transport (server-http.ts) and the Express /api/feature-flags routes that consume the same data, this is on the request hot path and prevents other requests from being served concurrently. Magnified because list_features, get_feature_info, set_feature_state and adjust_traffic_rollout ALL call readFeatures() on every call.
recommendation: Replace with fs.promises.readFile + cache the parsed JSON in memory with an mtime/fs.watch invalidation, or at minimum keep the file content in module-scope cache that is only re-read after a writeFeatures(). Same pattern needed in backend/routes/featureFlagRoutes.js (uses fs.promises but still reads-on-every-request).

issue: fs.writeFileSync + fs.renameSync on every state/traffic write
estimated_impact: Each set_feature_state / adjust_traffic_rollout call serializes the ENTIRE features.json (25 flags) to JSON and performs two synchronous disk operations (write + rename). Blocks event loop ~2-5ms per call under SSD, more under network FS. Under the HTTP MCP server this stalls every other concurrent request.
recommendation: Switch to fs.promises.writeFile + fs.promises.rename. Even better: write only the diffed flag, or move to a small SQLite/LMDB store if write frequency grows.

issue: features.json re-read from disk on every GET request, no Cache-Control header
evidence: router.get('/', protect, admin, asyncHandler(async (req, res) => { const raw = await fs.readFile(featuresFilePath, 'utf-8'); res.json(JSON.parse(raw)) }))
estimated_impact: Public GET /api/feature-flags/:name (line 22) is anonymous-callable; each request triggers a disk read + JSON.parse. A modest crawler doing 100 req/s costs 100 disk reads/s and 100 full 16KB parses/s, when the data changes only when an admin toggles a flag. Also no ETag / Cache-Control header so browsers/CDNs cannot cache.
recommendation: Cache parsed features in module scope, invalidate on PATCH; emit `Cache-Control: public, max-age=10` and an ETag (md5 of file mtime) so reverse proxies and the browser handle 304s. Note: this finding overlaps with security-findings (the public route also leaks unreleased-feature names — flag both).

issue: GET /api/orders returns ALL orders with no pagination and no projection
estimated_impact: Admin endpoint, but unbounded result set: with 10k orders each averaging 2KB (orderItems array), the response is ~20MB and forces Mongoose to hydrate 10k Document instances. p95 latency easily 2-10s; event-loop blocked while V8 serializes JSON. populate() additionally fans out to a second collection — efficient via $lookup-style batched query in Mongoose 5+ but still O(N) memory.
recommendation: Add ?pageNumber/?pageSize like getProducts already does; cap pageSize at 50; use .select('_id user totalPrice isPaid isDelivered createdAt') to avoid sending full orderItems arrays in a list view; add a compound index on (createdAt, user) if sorting is added.

issue: getMyOrders has no pagination or sort/limit
evidence: const orders = await Order.find({ user: req.user._id })
estimated_impact: A power user with hundreds of orders gets the entire history on every dashboard load. With 200 orders × 2KB ≈ 400KB transferred per request plus full Mongoose hydration. p95 grows linearly with order count; admins testing seed data won't notice the regression.
recommendation: Mirror the products pagination pattern (pageSize, pageNumber). Add an index on { user: 1, createdAt: -1 } and `.sort({ createdAt: -1 }).limit(pageSize).skip(pageSize*(page-1))`.

issue: getUsers returns full collection with no pagination, no projection, includes hashed password
estimated_impact: Admin endpoint, but unbounded — with 100k users each ~500B, response is ~50MB and the bcrypt hash is shipped for every user. JSON serialization of 100k docs blocks the event loop for >1s on Node. Compare to getUserById which correctly uses .select('-password').
recommendation: Add pagination + `.select('-password')`. Add a text index for admin search if filter is added.

issue: No index on Product.name despite $regex keyword search in productController.js:13
evidence: name: { type: String, required: true }  // no index defined; queried via $regex case-insensitive
estimated_impact: GET /api/products?keyword=foo runs Product.countDocuments({name:{$regex,$options:'i'}}) + Product.find(...) — both perform a full collection scan because a case-insensitive $regex without anchor cannot use a btree index. With 100k products, ~500ms-2s p95. The query also runs TWICE (countDocuments + find) — two full scans per request.
recommendation: Either (a) use MongoDB text index (`productSchema.index({name:'text'})`) and query with $text — sublinear with stemming; or (b) add a normalized lowercase `name_lower` field with a regular index and query with prefix-anchored regex (`^foo`); or (c) move to Atlas Search. Coordinate with security-mate: same line is ReDoS / NoSQL-injection vector.

issue: countDocuments + find issued as two separate queries instead of one aggregation
evidence: const count = await Product.countDocuments({ ...keyword }); const products = await Product.find({ ...keyword }).limit(pageSize).skip(...)
estimated_impact: Two round-trips per request: ~5-10ms wasted on every product list call. Worse, with $regex both queries scan the collection — duplicated work. Doubles MongoDB load on the products endpoint.
recommendation: Use a single $facet aggregation pipeline returning both the page and the count, or accept a stale count via $estimatedDocumentCount (sub-ms) when keyword is empty.

issue: Every protected request makes an extra User.findById round-trip
estimated_impact: Every authenticated API call costs one DB round-trip just to materialise req.user. With protect on /api/orders, /api/users/profile, /api/feature-flags, this is the single most-executed query on the backend. At 5ms per query × 50 req/s = 250ms/s of DB time wasted; ten authenticated users browsing simultaneously can starve a small MongoDB connection pool.
recommendation: Cache by JWT jti for the JWT TTL (or a short in-memory LRU keyed by user_id, 60s TTL); or push name/isAdmin into the JWT payload so the protect middleware only needs to verify, no DB hit. Today the token already contains _id only.

issue: product.reviews is an unbounded embedded array — document growth + recompute on every review
evidence: product.reviews.push(review); product.numReviews = product.reviews.length; product.rating = product.reviews.reduce((acc, item) => item.rating + acc, 0) / product.reviews.length
estimated_impact: MongoDB has a 16MB per-document hard cap. With ~200B per review, a popular product hits the cap around ~80k reviews and writes fail. Before that, the entire document is rewritten on every push (MongoDB rewrites docs that grow beyond their pre-allocated padding). The .reduce on every save is O(N) over all reviews; at 10k reviews the create-review endpoint p95 climbs into hundreds of ms.
recommendation: Move reviews into a separate collection with index on productId; keep rolling rating/numReviews counters on Product updated via $inc / running average. This is a classic embedded-vs-referenced trade-off worth an ADR — coordinate with architecture-mate.

issue: makeSnippet runs 8 regex passes over chunk text on every search hit
estimated_impact: Each MCP search returns top_k chunks (default 5, max 20). For each chunk this performs 9 full-text regex sweeps. The fenced-code regex /```[\s\S]*?```/g is non-greedy but unbounded — on a chunk with an unclosed ``` it scans the whole remaining text. Typical chunk ~2KB → ~0.1ms; max top_k=20 → ~2ms per search. Not catastrophic but easy to halve by combining passes or pre-computing snippets at index time.
recommendation: Pre-compute snippets at indexing time (chunker writes them as payload.snippet) and just return p.snippet here. Failing that, combine the regexes or limit work by slicing text to maxLen*3 before running them.

issue: Two sequential network round-trips per search (Ollama embed → Qdrant search) with no timeout
evidence: const res = await fetch(`${OLLAMA_URL}/api/embed`, ...); const response = await qdrant.search(COLLECTION, ...)
estimated_impact: Cold Ollama embed for nomic-embed-text is ~30-80ms; Qdrant search ~5-20ms. So baseline p50 ≈ 50-100ms per docs search. There is no AbortController/timeout on the fetch — if Ollama hangs, the MCP tool hangs forever and the upstream LLM call holds an open MCP session.
recommendation: Add an AbortController with a 5s timeout to the embed fetch; surface a SEARCH_TIMEOUT error so callers can retry. Consider a tiny LRU cache keyed by query string (most users repeat the same question multiple times).

issue: getTopProducts queried on every request with no caching
estimated_impact: Top-3 changes once a day at most but every homepage hit issues a sort over Product.rating with no index → full collection scan + in-memory sort. With 10k products that is ~50-100ms p95 per call, on a Public hot path.
recommendation: (a) Add an index on { rating: -1 }, dropping query to ~1ms; (b) wrap the controller in a 60s in-memory cache (lru-cache or a simple Map with TTL); (c) emit `Cache-Control: public, max-age=60` so browsers and CDN cache for free.

issue: Unbounded user-controlled $regex in MongoDB query (CPU + I/O cost)
estimated_impact: Beyond the security ReDoS risk (already filed by security-mate), this query forces a COLLSCAN — MongoDB cannot use the name btree even if one existed because case-insensitive non-anchored regex defeats the index. A malicious or naive `?keyword=.*` triggers a full scan every time. With 100k products: ~500ms-2s of CPU/IO per request.
recommendation: See N+1 finding for productController:20 — switch to $text index or normalized lowercase field. Also sanitize keyword length (cap at 64 chars) and escape regex meta-characters.

issue: jwt.verify is synchronous CPU work on every protected request
estimated_impact: HS256 verify is ~50-200µs — negligible per call, but it blocks the event loop and is called on every authenticated request. At 1000 req/s that is 50-200ms/s of blocking work. With RS256/ES256 the cost would jump 10-50× — keep HS256 for this reason.
recommendation: Acceptable today. Flag if the team ever migrates to asymmetric algorithms — then move verify to a worker_thread pool. Mostly informational.

issue: Mongoose 5.x is EOL and several deps are years out of date — patch + perf regressions left on the table
estimated_impact: Mongoose 6/7 has materially better query performance (lean by default in some paths, native driver upgrades). Worth ~10-20% on hot paths after upgrade. Caveat: documented Mongoose-5→6 migration risk in CLAUDE.md (`useCreateIndex` removal).
recommendation: Track via ADR. Out of scope for an isolated perf fix — coordinate with architecture-mate's dependency-upgrade ADR.

issue: product.reviews.reduce + .length called separately when both could share one pass
evidence: product.numReviews = product.reviews.length; product.rating = product.reviews.reduce((acc, item) => item.rating + acc, 0) / product.reviews.length
estimated_impact: Micro-optimisation; .length is O(1) on arrays so the cost is just the reduce. Not worth flagging in isolation, included only because the embedded-reviews design will hurt eventually (see medium finding above).
recommendation: Pair with the reviews-as-separate-collection refactor; do not optimise in isolation.
